title: The Eye
question: Which part of the eye is it?
lines: This is the white of your eye. What's it called?
Watch the tough outer layer that's glowing.
Which part of the eye is glowing?
The cornea is the clear window at the front, not this layer.
This tough white coat covers most of the eyeball.
It's B. The sclera.
Why it matters: the eye muscles attach to it to turn the eye.

title: The Eye
question: Which way does it turn the eye?
lines: Look right, then left. One muscle does the outward turn.
The glowing muscle is on the outer side of the right eye.
Which way does it turn the eye?
Its partner on the nose side pulls the eye the other way.
This muscle pulls the eye outward, away from the nose.
It's D. Away from the nose.
Why it matters: it's the only eye muscle run by cranial nerve six.

title: The Eye
question: What does the glowing part do?
lines: The colored part of your eye is doing a job right now.
Watch the glowing ring around the dark center.
What does the glowing part do?
Focusing is the job of the lens behind it.
The iris widens or narrows the pupil to let in more or less light.
It's C. It controls the light entering the eye.
Why it matters: it makes your pupils shrink in bright light.

title: The Eye
question: Which part of the eye is it?
lines: The front of your eye has a clear window.
Watch the glowing dome at the front of the eye.
Which part of the eye is it?
The iris is the colored ring behind it.
The glowing part is the transparent dome that covers the iris.
It's A. The cornea.
Why it matters: it does most of the eye's focusing.

title: The Eye
question: How many muscles move each eye?
lines: Your eyes move fast, all day long.
Watch the glowing muscles around the eyeball.
How many muscles move each eye?
Four rectus muscles and two oblique muscles.
That makes six on each eye.
It's B. Six muscles per eye.
Why it matters: they work together so both eyes can aim at the same spot.
